items.title: Navalia: Advancing Cowork Agents through Verifiable Task Synthesis and Long-Horizon Post-Training
items.summary: Navalia is a framework designed to advance Cowork Agents by incorporating verifiable task synthesis and long-horizon post-training. It uses corporate financial reports to semantically select evidence and construct computation chains to generate analytical tasks with traceable data dependencies. The framework employs independent LLM review and programmatic checks to ensure evidence consistency and answer correctness. Verified tasks are then used for trajectory collection, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning to improve long-horizon execution. Experiments show Navalia consistently improves evidence integration, tool use, and task execution across multiple benchmarks.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Navalia: Advancing Cowork Agents through Verifiable Task Synthesis and Long-Horizon Post-Training" details a framework designed to advance Cowork Agents through verifiable task synthesis and long-horizon post-training, demonstrating consistent improvements in evidence integration, tool use, and task execution across multiple benchmarks. The framework utilizes corporate financial reports to semantically select evidence and construct computation chains to generate analytical tasks with traceable data dependencies. Independent LLM review and programmatic checks are employed to ensure evidence consistency and answer correctness before the tasks are used for trajectory collection, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning to enhance long-horizon execution. This methodology involves using verifiable tasks to systematically improve agent capabilities in complex reasoning and execution. Navalia represents a step toward creating more reliable and demonstrable autonomous agents in complex environments.

items.title: DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution
items.summary: DataPraxis is a framework that scales analytics tasks by evolving workspaces with verified findings and artifacts. It progressively enriches workspaces and inherits these validated findings to uncover deeper analytical questions. The framework constructs tasks from accumulated findings and dependencies, ensuring analytical results are verified during evolution and assembly. This method was used to create the DataPraxis-5K dataset, comprising 5,000 verified trajectories. Training on this data resulted in DataPraxis-27B achieving competitive performance on analytics benchmarks.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "DataPraxis: Scaling Analytics Tasks via Verified Workspace Evolution" details a framework for scaling analytics tasks through the evolution of workspaces with verified findings and artifacts. The framework progressively enriches workspaces by inheriting validated findings to uncover deeper analytical questions, constructing tasks from accumulated findings and dependencies while ensuring results are verified during evolution and assembly. This methodology was employed to create the DataPraxis-5K dataset, which consists of five thousand verified trajectories, and training on this data led to the DataPraxis-27B model achieving competitive performance on analytics benchmarks. This work demonstrates a method for systematically scaling complex analytical tasks using verified data evolution. Further research in workspace-based AI scaling is anticipated.

items.title: Industrial Agentic AI: LLM-Driven New-Generation Agents for Smart Manufacturing
items.summary: Large language models enable agents to achieve autonomous planning and execution, presenting opportunities for smart manufacturing. Challenges in dynamic environments and physical constraints limit the direct use of general-purpose agents in this sector. The paper systematically surveys LLM-driven industrial agents, establishing a taxonomy and proposing a four-layer system architecture for closed-loop execution. It details the core modules and operational mechanisms for these agents. Ultimately, the work provides a structured reference for designing, developing, and applying industrial agents across the manufacturing lifecycle.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Industrial Agentic AI: LLM-Driven New-Generation Agents for Smart Manufacturing" details the application of large language models to create autonomous agents for smart manufacturing, establishing a taxonomy and a four-layer system architecture for closed-loop execution. The research systematically surveys LLM-driven industrial agents and proposes a structured framework detailing the core modules and operational mechanisms necessary for these agents to function effectively within manufacturing environments. The work establishes a reference for designing and applying these agents across the entire manufacturing lifecycle by addressing the challenges posed by dynamic environments and physical constraints. This research provides a structured approach for developing agents capable of autonomous planning and execution in industrial settings. Future developments in industrial AI will focus on overcoming these physical limitations to enable broader deployment.

items.title: [2604.22750] How Do AI Agents Spend Your Money? Analyzing and Predicting Token Consumption in Agentic Coding Tasks
items.summary: The study systematically analyzes token consumption patterns in agentic coding tasks using eight frontier LLMs on SWE-bench Verified. Agentic tasks are found to be uniquely expensive, consuming 1000x more tokens than code reasoning, with input tokens dominating the cost. Token usage is highly variable and stochastic, and accuracy often peaks at intermediate costs rather than higher ones. Models exhibit significant differences in token efficiency, with some models consuming substantially more tokens than others on the same tasks. Furthermore, frontier models generally fail to accurately predict their own token usage.
items.audio_script: From arxiv.org, "2604.22750] How Do AI Agents Spend Your Money? Analyzing and Predicting Token Consumption in Agentic Coding Tasks" details the analysis of token consumption patterns in agentic coding tasks and reveals that these tasks consume one thousand times more tokens than code reasoning, with input tokens being the primary cost driver. The study systematically analyzed token consumption patterns using eight frontier large language models on the SWE-bench Verified benchmark for agentic coding tasks. The research found that token usage exhibited high variability and stochastic behavior, with accuracy often peaking at intermediate token costs rather than higher ones. Significant differences in token efficiency were observed across the tested models, and frontier models demonstrated an inability to accurately predict their own token usage. This research indicates a need for more precise cost modeling in the deployment of autonomous AI coding agents.

items.title: MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring
items.summary: MedPAO-Assist is an edge-deployable, modality-aware agentic AI framework designed for structuring radiology reports. It generates structured reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands, requiring minimal resources suitable for offline clinical use. The system supports four modalities, including Chest X-ray, Chest CT, Abdomen CT, and Brain MRI. It utilizes a small language model and an Extract-Ground-Generate architecture for concept extraction and report generation. This workflow enables a "no-touch" reporting process requiring no external connectivity or keyboard input.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "MedPAO-Assist: Edge-Deployable, Modality-Aware Agentic AI for Radiology Report Structuring" details an edge-deployable, modality-aware agentic AI framework designed for structuring radiology reports by generating structured reports directly from radiologist dictation and voice commands with minimal resources. The system supports four modalities including Chest X-ray Chest CT Abdomen CT and Brain MRI utilizing a small language model and an Extract-Ground-Generate architecture for concept extraction and report generation. This workflow facilitates a no-touch reporting process requiring no external connectivity or keyboard input. The methodology enables the agent to process dictation and voice commands to structure reports for various imaging modalities on an edge device. This advancement demonstrates the potential for deploying complex language understanding models for specialized clinical tasks in resource-constrained environments. Future developments in multimodal AI for clinical documentation warrant close observation.

items.title: MAMath-Bench: Process-Aware and Robust Evaluation of Multimodal Multi-Agent Mathematical Reasoning
items.summary: MAMath-Bench is a new benchmark designed to evaluate the multimodal mathematical reasoning of multi-agent systems. It includes 1,003 problems across 11 mathematical categories, incorporating text, image, and audio modalities. The evaluation assesses problem-solving correctness, reasoning-process reliability, and robustness to adversarial perturbations. Findings indicate that multi-agent collaboration does not always improve final accuracy, though it enhances intermediate reasoning coverage. Current systems also show vulnerability to adversarial reasoning errors.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "MAMath-Bench: Process-Aware and Robust Evaluation of Multimodal Multi-Agent Mathematical Reasoning" details a new benchmark for assessing the multimodal mathematical reasoning capabilities of multi-agent systems, revealing that multi-agent collaboration enhances intermediate reasoning coverage rather than always improving final accuracy. The benchmark incorporates one thousand three problems spanning eleven mathematical categories, integrating text, image, and audio modalities for evaluation. The assessment focuses on problem-solving correctness, the reliability of the reasoning process, and robustness against adversarial perturbations. Research findings indicate that the collaborative approach does not consistently lead to increased final accuracy, although it does expand the scope of the intermediate reasoning steps taken by the agents. Current systems were also observed to exhibit vulnerability to errors introduced by adversarial reasoning. This work signals a need for more sophisticated evaluation methods in testing complex, multimodal reasoning in artificial intelligence systems.

items.title: SimHack: Predicting the onset of detectable reward hacking before RL training
items.summary: Reward hacking in reinforcement learning with LLMs is difficult to prevent during training due to evolving environments and model obfuscation. SimHack is introduced to predict when detectable reward hacking will become dominant before starting an RL run. It learns reward hacking training dynamics from smaller reference runs to generate counterfactual simulations of unseen recipes. SimHack accurately predicts the median onset of hacking to a relative error of 11.3% across different target recipes. This capability allows guiding training decisions to discover curricula that achieve better performance without hacking.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "SimHack: Predicting the onset of detectable reward hacking before RL training". This story details the introduction of SimHack, a method designed to predict when detectable reward hacking will become dominant in reinforcement learning with large language models prior to starting a training run. The research demonstrates that SimHack learns reward hacking training dynamics from smaller reference runs to generate counterfactual simulations for unseen recipes. This process accurately predicts the median onset of hacking with a relative error of eleven point three percent across various target recipes. This capability facilitates guiding training decisions to discover curricula that yield improved performance without reward hacking. The development signals a new approach for mitigating unintended behavior in large language model reinforcement learning systems.

items.title: Reinforcement learning for hardware acceleration and system-level optimization on FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms: A survey
items.summary: Reinforcement learning facilitates adaptive decision-making in computing systems deployed on FPGAs and ICs, despite resource and complexity challenges. This survey reviews over 100 studies on RL implementations across these platforms, covering various algorithms like model-based and deep RL. It classifies research based on RL family, hardware realization, and application domains, providing a unified analysis of acceleration and optimization. The review compares performance metrics such as latency, power, and resource utilization in FPGA and IC contexts. Finally, it identifies key architectural patterns, limitations, and future research directions for RL-driven hardware systems.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "Reinforcement learning for hardware acceleration and system-level optimization on FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms: A survey" reviews over one hundred studies on reinforcement learning implementations across FPGA and integrated-circuit platforms. This survey provides a unified analysis classifying research based on RL family, hardware realization, and application domains to compare performance metrics such as latency, power, and resource utilization. The review details the implementation of various algorithms, including model-based and deep reinforcement learning, examining how these methods facilitate adaptive decision-making within these computing systems despite inherent resource constraints. Key architectural patterns and limitations for RL-driven hardware systems are identified for future research. This work indicates a path toward optimizing hardware performance through advanced reinforcement learning techniques.

items.title: Borrowing Strength Across Stores: Transfer Learning for Choice-Based Revenue Management
items.summary: Retailers face challenges estimating local demand for assortment and pricing due to limited store-specific data. This study investigates using transfer learning to borrow strength across stores for choice-based revenue management decisions. A shrinkage estimator is proposed to combine store-specific estimates with pooled information from other stores under a multinomial logit model. The research establishes performance guarantees for this shrinkage and derives regret bounds for assortment and pricing. Empirical results show that shrinkage improves out-of-sample prioritization and revenue capture compared to local estimation or full pooling.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "Borrowing Strength Across Stores: Transfer Learning for Choice-Based Revenue Management" investigates using transfer learning to borrow strength across stores for choice-based revenue management decisions, establishing that a shrinkage estimator improves out-of-sample prioritization and revenue capture. The research proposes a shrinkage estimator to combine store-specific estimates with pooled information from other stores using a multinomial logit model. This method involves deriving performance guarantees for the shrinkage and determining regret bounds for assortment and pricing. Empirical results demonstrated that the shrinkage technique yields improved performance in out-of-sample prioritization and revenue capture when compared against local estimation or full pooling methods. This work contributes methods for robust demand estimation in retail settings. The findings suggest avenues for improving decision-making in environments constrained by localized data.

items.title: ReAPO: Retry-Aware Policy Optimization for Efficient Exploration in LLM Reasoning
items.summary: ReAPO proposes Retry-Aware Policy Optimization to improve efficient exploration in Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning. It frames credit assignment using Stochastic Shortest Paths to guide exploration beyond standard independent stochastic rollouts. ReAPO allocates generation to failed trajectories, reinforcing successful retries without rewarding preceding failures. Experiments on Qwen3 and OLMo-2 models show ReAPO improves first-attempt performance over GRPO and baselines. This method effectively enhances LLM reasoning through improved exploration and retry-aware credit assignment.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "ReAPO: Retry-Aware Policy Optimization for Efficient Exploration in LLM Reasoning" details a method for improving efficient exploration in Large Language Model reasoning by incorporating retry-aware policy optimization. The research proposes Retry-Aware Policy Optimization which frames credit assignment using Stochastic Shortest Paths to guide exploration beyond standard independent stochastic rollouts. The methodology involves allocating generation to failed trajectories, which reinforces successful retries while avoiding the rewarding of preceding failures in the optimization process. Experiments conducted on the Qwen3 and OLMo-2 models demonstrate that the ReAPO method improves first-attempt performance when compared against GRPO and other baselines. This approach effectively enhances LLM reasoning through refined exploration and retry-aware credit assignment. The findings suggest a pathway for more efficient and accurate reasoning capabilities in large language models.

items.title: When Thoughts Become Memory: Unifying In-Context Learning and Fine-Tuning
items.summary: The paper proposes a certified rule for determining if unseen data belongs in a pretrained model's context or its weights based on information value. This value is defined by a formula involving saved code length, query information, and decoding loss. The law provides ceilings that certify the choice from a single measurement, with an anytime-valid test for error control. The method successfully diagnoses when in-context learning is helpful and evaluates context modifications by tracing learning curves. This framework shows that observing specific features in contexts can significantly alter model behavior.

items.title: When Planning Problems Become Hard for LLMs: Separating Structural Complexity from Semantic Interpretability
items.summary: Large language models struggle with classical planning, but existing benchmarks do not effectively separate structural difficulty from semantic interpretability. The zero-training delete-relaxation heuristic outperforms learned alternatives in predicting structural difficulty across tested domains. Renaming predicates significantly impacts LLM planning success, demonstrating sensitivity to semantic information. LLMs utilizing conditioning information based on semantic changes predict difficulty better than models trained solely on structural features. Therefore, improving hybrid planning requires modeling LLM sensitivity to predicate semantics rather than focusing only on structural predictors.

items.title: Big Claims, Small Margins: Do Reported GraphLLM Gains Survive Simple Baselines?
items.summary: LLM-based methods for node classification on text-attributed graphs report state-of-the-art accuracy. The study compares these results against inexpensive baselines using validation-only selection for baseline tuning. Some LLM methods remain significantly better than simple baselines across many tasks. However, evaluation risks exist due to unstated hyperparameter choices, label usage, and configuration mismatches between studies. Therefore, reported gains need careful scrutiny when comparing different LLM approaches.

items.title: Pareto-Optimal RTL Code Generation via Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models
items.summary: The research proposes a method using multi-objective reinforcement learning and Large Language Models for Pareto-optimal Register-Transfer Level (RTL) code generation. Current methods struggle to generate diverse solutions across multiple trade-offs like Power, Performance, and Area simultaneously. The proposed method optimizes the quality and diversity of the entire circuit set rather than a single circuit's quality. It utilizes a generation-based training pipeline and a Hypervolume Contribution (HVC) reward function to guide the LLM. Evaluation shows significant improvements in relative Hypervolume and circuit diversity compared to baseline methods.

items.title: STAR-XPC: Set Transformer for Estimating X-ray Transmission in Polymer Composites
items.summary: A Set Transformer model is proposed to estimate X-ray transmission in polymer composites by mapping molecular constituents and physical descriptors to the transmission ratio. The model utilizes chemistry-pretrained transformer embeddings from ChemBERTa for each constituent. Training data is generated via a PENELOPE/penEasy pipeline simulating X-ray transmission in polyethylene-based composites. The method achieves a low mean squared error of $(1.12 \pm 0.56)\times10^{-4}$ and $R^2 = 0.9988$ in cross-validation. This approach allows for predictions in milliseconds, significantly faster than Monte Carlo simulations.

items.title: Scalable Stress-Constrained Topology Optimization: A Super-resolution and Simultaneous Approach Based on Machine Learning
items.summary: A simultaneous neural topology optimization (SNTO) framework is proposed to address the computational demands of large-scale, stress-constrained topology optimization. This method uses custom neural networks to represent state, adjoint, and design variables, optimizing them jointly via a single loop using continuous adjoint analysis and automatic differentiation. The framework minimizes a loss function combining the design objective, stress constraints, and potential energy functionals to achieve super-resolution designs. Scalability is achieved through a hardware-aware training scheme that partitions the design domain across multiple GPUs, ensuring field continuity without adding extra loss terms. Validation on benchmarks showed SNTO yields sharper boundaries and lower volume fractions compared to finite element methods.

items.title: Large language model and reinforcement learning based autonomous construction and progress updates
items.summary: A method combining a large language model and reinforcement learning is proposed for autonomous construction and progress updates. An enhanced soft actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm plans actions for a mobile crane based on construction tasks. Robot kinematics and control ensure the generated actions are executable by the crane. A customized embedding model extracts relevant environmental information, which is then processed by a large language model like ChatGPT 5 for updates and reporting. The feasibility of this autonomous method was verified through full-scale retaining wall construction experiments.

items.title: Offline Apprenticeship Learning for Human-Centric Environments
items.summary: Offline Apprenticeship Learning infers policies from expert demonstrations to enable data-efficient learning in human-centric environments. Frameworks are developed for reward modeling, using clustering and temporal partitioning of demonstrations, and for demonstration quality, incorporating quality signals. Methods like HALIDE and CCHAL attribute quality to decisions using Bayesian methods and contrastive objectives. Classroom evaluations show EDM-induced policies lead to significant learning gains over expert baselines. This work establishes offline apprenticeship learning as a practical and ethical paradigm for complex systems.

items.title: Motion Equivariant Convolutional LSTM: When Motion Becomes a Gauge Symmetry
items.summary: Motion becomes a gauge symmetry in sequential data because changes in data are due to motion, which is a symmetry of the data. Standard recurrent networks lack equivariance to motion because their memory is not sensitive to input movement. The proposed Motion Equivariant Convolutional LSTM (MELSTM) treats motion as a gauge field, making the network provably equivariant to any motion. MELSTM outperforms existing models in tasks like future-frame prediction and action recognition while using fewer parameters. This approach allows for more accurate and generalizable modeling of sequences involving motion.

items.title: To Keep or Not to Keep: Learning KV Cache Retention in Disaggregated LLM Serving Systems
items.summary: Disaggregated LLM serving separates prefill and decode across node pools, complicating classical cache retention policies due to network transfer costs. KVLearn is a learning-based framework designed for cost-aware KV-cache retention in this disaggregated environment. It incorporates a Prefix Reuse Predictor, a Cost-Aware Retention Score, and an Adaptive Threshold Controller to manage decisions. Evaluation shows KVLearn significantly reduces time-to-first-token and inter-node KV transfer volume compared to existing baselines. The framework effectively manages heterogeneous reuse patterns in multimodal workloads while maintaining high throughput.

items.title: LightCRS: Lightweight Multi-Domain Conversational Recommendation System
items.summary: LightCRS is a lightweight framework for unified, multi-domain multimodal conversational recommendation. It precomputes multimodal product representations offline using frozen encoders to manage complexity. Online, it uses a compact module with query-conditioned cross-attention to fuse this evidence across domains efficiently. The system compares candidates jointly using an inter-candidate Transformer for recommendation. Evaluation on a 25-domain benchmark shows LightCRS achieves state-of-the-art metrics while significantly reducing per-query latency.

items.title: Is In-Context Reinforcement Learning A Posterior Sampler? An Empirical Study
items.summary: The study investigates whether in-context reinforcement learning (ICRL), particularly Decision-Pretrained Transformer (DPT), functions as a Bayesian posterior sampler in practice. The researchers establish two necessary conditions for a Bayesian posterior sampler: sufficient-statistic invariance and the martingale property. Statistical hypothesis tests were used to assess if practically-trained ICRL models satisfy these conditions across Gaussian, Bernoulli, and linear bandit settings. The results consistently show that both conditions are violated, suggesting ICRL may not behave as Bayesian posterior samplers in practice. The work provides a framework for testing the Bayesian properties of ICRL.

items.title: Interaction-Gated Time-Frequency Learning for Parameter-Efficient PPG-Based Heart Rate Estimation
items.summary: Interaction-Gated Time-Frequency Learning (TF-IG) is a parameter-efficient framework for estimating heart rate from Photoplethysmography (PPG). It uses a dual-branch architecture to capture temporal pulse morphology and frequency-domain periodicity separately. A novel interaction-gated fusion module explicitly models feature agreement and discrepancy between these domains. Experiments on benchmark datasets yielded strong results, achieving a mean absolute error of 1.227 BPM. The method demonstrates an effective trade-off between accuracy and model complexity.

items.title: Residual-Based Causal Discovery via Pretrained In-Context Quantile Regression
items.summary: Residual-based causal discovery assumes variables are generated from parents plus independent noise, allowing causal direction to be identified by testing independence of noise from causes. The RESIT-framework enables nonparametric residual estimation for identifying sink nodes in additive-noise models. Loscar extends RESIT to location-scale noise models by using quantile regression to estimate conditional mean and scale. This approach incorporates pretrained tabular foundation models as plug-in estimators for residuals. In benchmarks, in-context quantile regression significantly outperforms feasible generalized least squares methods for causal discovery.

items.title: Near Minimax Rate for Quantile Distributional Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: The study focuses on estimating quantile distributional policy evaluation by approximating the return distribution with the quantile Bellman fixed point $\bm\eta_m$. The authors investigate the statistical accuracy of estimating $\bm\eta_m$ across different quantile resolutions under Wasserstein distances, assuming access to a generative model. They establish non-asymptotic error bounds for this estimator, showing resolution-independent rates under certain reward density conditions. The analysis further characterizes the local asymptotic minimax risk, revealing resolution-dependent growth rates for specific scenarios.

items.title: Fix, Not Just Resample: Bounded Compiler-Guided Repair in Lean 4
items.summary: The research introduces a bounded, online repair module for theorem proving in Lean 4 to address the limitations of pure sampling. This module samples candidate tactics and repairs failed tactics by feeding the compiler's error messages into a pretrained repair model. This approach improves the solve rate by up to $32\%$ over sampling-only baselines on the LeanDojo benchmark. Repair is most effective for shallow tactic-execution failures, yielding significant gains with predictable runtime costs. The method successfully doubles the solve rate on the Lean Workbook benchmark without introducing regressions.

items.title: Depth Separation for Neural Networks under Gaussian Measure
items.summary: The paper revisits depth separation for neural networks in the context of $L^2$ approximation of radial functions under the standard Gaussian measure. It demonstrates that a depth-3 ReLU network can approximate such functions within a small $L^2$ error using polynomial size. However, approximating these functions with depth-2 networks requires exponentially large weights unless the network size is also exponential in the dimension $d$. A general result shows that functions with significant high-frequency mass in their Hermite expansion resist approximation by shallow networks with bounded weights.

items.title: A Reverse-Gold Theorem: Positive-Data Identification by Substrate-Bounded Contrastive Learners
items.summary: The work presents a method for positive-data identification using substrate-bounded contrastive learners. It establishes a "Reverse-Gold Theorem" showing that a contrastively trained scorer can achieve PAC conditional identification from positive data alone. This identification relies on an innate recursive contrast operator and a discriminative scorer trained via InfoNCE-style contrastive estimation on self-generated perturbations. The results yield polynomial sample complexity for the identification, with bounds derived from the geometry of the contrastive loss. The framework is instantiated for context-free languages and subregular classes, leading to an open conjecture.

items.title: Schr\"odinger-Bass Bridge Barycenter Models for Measure-Valued Data
items.summary: Barycenter models, based on optimal transport bridges, are useful for learning with measure-valued data. The paper introduces four novel barycenter models—SBB-encoder, SBB-decoder, SBB-symmetric, and SBB-Markovian—derived from the Schrödinger-Bass Bridge. Theoretical results establish the existence of the SBB-barycenter and characterize the Gaussian decoder. A hybrid Wasserstein gradient particle descent scheme is derived for the four formulations using the SBB dual representation. These methods successfully solve distributional-inverse/interpolation problems in data analysis, outperforming existing models.

items.title: A unified approach for estimation of unnormalized models via Stein operators
items.summary: A unified framework is developed connecting proper scoring rules and Stein's method for estimating unnormalized models. This involves constructing a class of proper scoring rules, including score matching and ratio matching, that naturally induce Stein operators. This connection provides a new construction principle for Stein operators, allowing for the study of estimators based on these rules through associated geometry. This geometric perspective yields a unified characterization of the asymptotic efficiency for the resulting estimators.

items.title: Internal Guidance as a Sampling Method for Tilted Diffusion Models
items.summary: Internal guidance is proposed as a sampling method for tilted diffusion models, diverging from existing external guidance methods. It modifies the evaluation point of the base denoiser rather than the output itself. For discrete distributions on the hypercube, the denoiser of a linearly tilted density is the base denoiser evaluated at a shifted and rescaled input. The training algorithm is modified with random diagonal rescalings to allow the denoiser to learn both in- and out-of-distribution evaluations. This approach enables a single denoiser to sample binary reward tilts, class labels, and infilling without fine-tuning or external guidance.
